text:
incident-bot: PAGER -> KV cache eviction spike on inference-runtime-1. Error rate rising to ~7%, 90th latency +220ms. Trigger condition: large structured function/tool invocations (schema arrays) causing batch fragmentation and prefix KV misses. Auto-notification to #incidents.

maya: I’m on call, looking. Paging SRE.

jon: Seen it in logs — continuous-batcher is creating many tiny batches when payloads include nested `results` arrays and `tool_invocations`. The batching key (prefix hash) varies because we serialize structured output differently across requests -> cache keys diverge and KV grows until evictions spike.

eva: Confirming. Grep from runtime logs:
```
[runtime] 2024-02-09T14:12:03Z batcher: shard=2 size=1 keys=[a1b2] payload_schema=complex-array
[cache] 2024-02-09T14:12:03Z kv: miss key=a1b2 reason=prefix-variance
[evict] 2024-02-09T14:12:07Z store=kv-1 evicted=256MB threshold=80%
[metrics] 2024-02-09T14:12:10Z errors=45 latency_p90=420ms
```

liam: Looks like a recent rollout of the structured-output encoder in canary caused the change in serialization ordering. Propose emergency mitigation: 1) disable continuous batching for the affected route, OR 2) force canonical serialization (not trivial in runtime), OR 3) lower `max_batch_tokens` to force larger coalesced batches. Fastest is toggling batching for the route to reduce prefix churn.

maya: I’ll do the toggle. Which route names?

jon: Routes: `/v1/chat/generate` (canary) and `/v1/tool/exec` (traffic spike). Start with `/v1/tool/exec`.

liam: Command to apply via operator API:
```bash
curl -X POST https://control-plane/api/v1/routes/config \
  -H "Authorization: Bearer $TOKEN" \
  -d '{"route":"/v1/tool/exec","continuous_batching":false}'
```

maya: Running it now. @deploy-bot please apply.

deploy-bot: Applying runtime change: route=/v1/tool/exec continuous_batching=false by maya. Change id=chg-20240209-001.

deploy-bot: Done. Propagated to runtime pool (shard 0-3) ~12s ago.

jon: Watching metrics: errors dropping from 7% -> 2% in last 60s, p90 latency trending down. Dashboard: https://dash.redwood/boards/kv-evict?range=15m

paul: Customer impact: flagged by 3 customers on Dedicated clusters. All reported latency spikes and one support ticket about timeouts. No data corruption. Let support know mitigation in progress.

eva: Post-mortem notes — root cause hypothesis: non-deterministic serialization of structured tool outputs changed cache key distribution after canary encoder. We should add canonical serializer in ingress or normalize before hashing.

liam: Temporary follow-up: schedule rollback of structured-output encoder in canary until canonicalization landed. Also add a guard in batcher: if batch fragmentation rate > 30% within 2m, auto-disable continuous batching for that route.

maya: Assigning follow-ups: liam -> rollback canary; eva -> add canonicalization ticket; jon -> implement batcher guard alert; paul -> update customers and close tickets if no further regressions.

maya: Handing off to day SRE for monitoring and postmortem. Oncall clear. :thumbsup:

incident-bot: Incident updated: severity=sev2, status=mitigated. Links: runbook/kv-cache-batcher, changelist/chg-20240209-001
